_about: Hand-edited neighborhood settings, merged into assets/neighborhoods.json by tools/build-neighborhoods.mjs. Keys are the City's neighborhood names. status: downtown | pilot | done | todo (default) | outside (automatic). profile: a key of profiles. named: real buildings to style and label.

pilsen-brick.about: Red and brown brick 2-3 flats and worker cottages, cream-brick storefronts, stone churches, brick and concrete warehouses by the river

worker-cottage.about: Frame and brick worker cottages with pitched roofs, painted siding, brick two-flats, corner taverns and churches; industry along the river

greystone-flats.about: Greystone and brick two- and three-flats, brick apartment courts, mansions on the boulevards

chinatown.about: Painted and red brick storefronts and walk-ups, newer mid-rises

brick-two-flat.about: Brick two- and three-flats, frame cottages, corner storefronts, converted lofts

lincoln-brownstone.about: Greystones, brownstones and brick three-flats, frame cottages, courtyard buildings, lakefront high-rises

loft-district.about: Brick warehouse lofts, newer glass and concrete mid- and high-rises

campus.about: University campus: modernist concrete and brick halls, older brick houses around it

lakefront-highrise.about: Greystone and brownstone row houses and mansions among lakefront apartment towers

loop-masonry.about: The Loop: terracotta, limestone and brick Chicago School office blocks, Art Deco towers, modern glass skyscrapers

streeterville-glass.about: Streeterville and the Magnificent Mile: limestone and greystone pre-war towers, lakefront glass and concrete high-rises

printers-row-brick.about: Printers Row: brick and terracotta printing lofts

_profiles: Each profile is a list of rules; a building takes the first rule it matches (minArea/maxArea in m2, maxH in m). families maps FAMILIES indices (js/city-data.js) to weights; roof is flat, gable (small near-rectangular houses: ridge at the measured height) or cornice (parapet trim).
_named: named: real Cook County footprints (id = objectId-part) located from OpenStreetMap (osm, ODbL) and given a facade family; kind picks the label icon. Churches rise to their nave with a pitched roof, and their tower(s) (twin: true) stand at the front (N/E/S/W, visually estimated) reaching the measured height.
_raisedRails: raisedRails: OSM line names that run on an embankment here (OSM rarely tags embankments); streets pass under them through viaducts.
_families: FAMILIES (js/city-data.js): 0-5 downtown mix (0 beige stone, 1 brown brick, 2 pale stone, 3 blue glass, 4 dark glass, 5 concrete); 6 red brick; 7 brown brick; 8 cream brick; 9 greystone; 10 church stone; 11 siding; 12 siding blue-grey; 13 siding sand; 14 greystone light; 15 greystone dark; 16 frame white; 17 frame mint; 18 frame blue; 19 frame yellow; 20 yellow brick; 21 brownstone; 22 Chinatown brick; 23 loft brick; 24 modernist concrete; 25 lakefront glass; 26 greenhouse glass.
_downtownNamed: Downtown buildings (assets/downtown.json) get their labels in the downtown touch-up: Field Museum 928203-0, Adler Planetarium 928439-0, NEMA 927184-0, One Museum Park West 927054-0.
